docs.hero.issue.agent.text: Agents cannot tell which visible node is safe to edit.
docs.hero.issue.ir.label: Issue 01
docs.hero.issue.ir.text: Design IR drifts away from the shipped web files.

docs.hero.issue.review.text: Reviews happen on exported artifacts instead of source changes.
docs.hero.lead: OpenGraphite opens the Web source files themselves. Standard CSS owns design values, while optional metadata is limited to identity, component and node references, bindings, editing policy, and resource provenance that the Web implementation cannot reconstruct. No OpenGraphite-reserved custom-property namespace remains in authored source.
docs.hero.title: Design tools, code, and agents should not edit different sources of truth.
docs.list.app.body: Web source files are the editable source of truth. The app layers editing affordances on top of WebKit instead of converting pages into a separate design IR.
docs.list.app.title: Design philosophy
docs.list.cli.body: Agents should inspect the .ogp scope, query nodes, make node-level edits, validate, and capture screenshots before handing work back.
docs.list.cli.title: Agent workflow
docs.list.css.body: Tags and standard attributes carry meaning, while standard CSS properties own design values and rendering rules. Optional metadata is limited to identity, references, bindings, editing policy, and resource provenance; .ogp stores project metadata and preview mocks.
docs.list.css.meta: optional identity / display / grid / position / standard CSS properties
docs.list.css.title: Source-of-truth contract
docs.list.mcp.body: Pages may keep lightweight og-instance references. OpenGraphite.runtime.js expands them for preview; ogkiln build expands them for static distribution. Generated DOM is not the source.
docs.list.mcp.title: Runtime and build boundary

docs.ops.audience.contributor.body: Only the appendix covers changing and building the OpenGraphite repository itself.
docs.ops.audience.user.body: Sections 1–9 are the operating guide for people who open and edit projects. Start here.
docs.ops.components.body: A registered hyphenated Custom Element owns a direct template. Pages keep lightweight og-instance references and use native slot, part, variant, class, and ARIA semantics.
docs.ops.components.preview.body: Preview values are projected only onto generated clones. They never enter source HTML or static build output. Internal-ID lookup wins; display-ID is fallback only, and both entries are never merged.
docs.ops.components.preview.title: Preview state belongs to the canvas manifest
docs.ops.components.title: Keep components source-first
docs.ops.contract.body: OpenGraphite edits ordinary Web source. Standard HTML carries structure and meaning; standard CSS carries rendering values; .ogp carries project and canvas metadata.
docs.ops.contract.css: Store design values in standard properties. Shared project tokens are ordinary custom properties in the configured cssLibrary.
docs.ops.contract.generated: Runtime-expanded DOM, screenshots, and static build output are derived artifacts. Review and edit their source resources instead.
docs.ops.contract.html: Use semantic tags, standard attributes, and readable fallback content. Optional data-og-id and data-og-internal-id exist only where collaboration needs stable identity.
docs.ops.contract.ogp: Store registration, canvas placement, viewport, guides, annotations, references, and preview mocks. Do not duplicate page DOM or design values.
docs.ops.contract.title: Keep one editable source of truth
docs.ops.contributors.body: This appendix is only for people developing the OpenGraphite application or repository. It is not required to open and edit a project as an end user.
docs.ops.contributors.check.gate: Complete Scripts/quality_gate.sh successfully before handing off repository changes.
docs.ops.contributors.check.project: Change project.yml when project generation changes; treat OpenGraphite.xcodeproj as generated output.
docs.ops.contributors.check.sync: Synchronize implementation, tests, specifications, user documentation, skills, and Tutorials in one change.
docs.ops.contributors.notice.body: Use project.yml as the XcodeGen source of truth and never edit OpenGraphite.xcodeproj directly. Keep implementation, tests, documentation, skills, and Tutorials synchronized in the same change.
docs.ops.contributors.notice.title: Contributor boundary
docs.ops.contributors.title: Contributor appendix: change OpenGraphite itself
docs.ops.done.body: The operation is complete only when another person or agent can reopen the same project, understand why the change is safe, and continue from the same source of truth.
docs.ops.done.title: The source diff, validation result, and rendered evidence agree.
docs.ops.edit.adopt.title: Adopt only when stable identity is needed
docs.ops.edit.body: Prefer text, attribute, style, insert, move, or copy operations over whole-document replacement. Each command revalidates its target and writes atomically.
docs.ops.edit.cssguard.body: Before node style set/remove, inspect the same active media conditions and require complete CSS provenance for that target. Never bypass incomplete-css-provenance-write-blocked by editing generated output.
docs.ops.edit.cssguard.title: CSS write guard
docs.ops.edit.title: Make the smallest supported edit
docs.ops.edit.write.title: Use the operation that matches the capability
docs.ops.i18n.body: Keep readable fallback text in HTML, translations in locale JSON, and locale typography in standard root font-family and :lang() rules.
docs.ops.i18n.title: Keep text resources and typography explicit
docs.ops.inspect.body: Resolve the project scope, validate registered resources, inspect the page graph, and query by capability. Copy returned ogref values; do not invent IDs.
docs.ops.inspect.step.diagnostics: Treat error diagnostics as blockers. Review warnings before selecting an operation.
docs.ops.inspect.step.reference: Use a stable ogref for writes. Explicitly adopt a session reference only when a stable collaboration target is required.
docs.ops.inspect.step.scope: Confirm the resolved root, htmlRoot, cssLibrary, Chapters, Collections, pages, and components.
docs.ops.inspect.title: Inspect before every write
docs.ops.mcp.body: The stdio MCP server delegates write tools to Scripts/ogkiln. App, CLI, MCP, humans, and agents therefore share validation, diagnostics, source resolution, and atomic write behavior.
docs.ops.mcp.note: Read operations never add annotation. Mutation tools require an explicit project and stable target, and return the same structured diagnostics as the CLI.
docs.ops.mcp.title: Use MCP through the same Core
docs.ops.nav.label: FOR END USERS
docs.ops.start.body: Install OpenGraphite from the Downloads guide, launch the App, then choose Open Sample Project or open your own .ogp project. Opening and previewing a project never rewrite its Web source.
docs.ops.start.check.app: The intended .ogp project opens and its registered pages appear on the canvas.
docs.ops.start.check.clean: Opening, previewing, and inspecting have not added annotations or changed source files.
docs.ops.start.check.project: The displayed Project and Public paths resolve to the source you intend to edit.
docs.ops.start.requirements.body: Use the App for visual editing. Use ogkiln CLI for repeatable inspection and automation, and MCP when an AI client must use the same validated operations. All three interfaces share the same Core contract.
docs.ops.start.requirements.title: Choose the interface that matches your work
docs.ops.start.step.confirm: Confirm the Project and Public paths shown in the header before inspecting or writing any source.
docs.ops.start.step.install: Install and launch OpenGraphite by following the Downloads guide.
docs.ops.start.step.open: Choose Open Sample Project to learn the workflow, or open the .ogp file for the project you intend to edit.
docs.ops.start.title: Open a project in OpenGraphite
docs.ops.summary: This runbook is primarily for people using OpenGraphite through the App, ogkiln CLI, or MCP. It covers opening, inspecting, editing, validating, and delivering a project from one Web source of truth. Repository development is isolated in the contributor appendix.
docs.ops.title: OpenGraphite operations documentation
docs.ops.trouble.attribute: Use a contract-editable standard attribute appropriate for the selected tag and content model.
docs.ops.trouble.body: Do not retry a blocked write with broader access or edit generated output. Resolve the source condition, inspect again, then issue a new minimal operation.
docs.ops.trouble.capability: Re-query the node and choose an operation supported by its current capability evidence.
docs.ops.trouble.css: Resolve unreadable/external stylesheets, imports, unsupported selectors, or the target-level provenance gap before a CSS write.
docs.ops.trouble.readonly: Move ownership to a writable source explicitly; removal never guesses across a read-only winner.
docs.ops.trouble.specificity: Edit the authored writable winner or redesign the selector; do not force a broader override.
docs.ops.trouble.title: Treat diagnostics as operating boundaries
docs.ops.verify.body: A successful write is not the finish line. Validate the project, capture the affected page or node, and produce a static build when delivery matters. Repository contributors run the additional quality gate listed in the appendix.
docs.ops.verify.check.build.body: Static output contains no .ogp metadata and preserves component/slot semantics.
docs.ops.verify.check.diff.body: Only the intended Web source and project metadata changed; generated output is not treated as editable source.
docs.ops.verify.check.validation.body: No error diagnostics; every warning is reviewed and explained.
docs.ops.verify.check.visual.body: The affected viewport, locale, state, and responsive condition match the intended result.
docs.ops.verify.title: Verify the source and the rendered result
docs.spec.commands.body: ogkiln covers contract reads, explicit migration, project registration, document context, page/component graphs, i18n resources, validation, build output, screenshots, and node-level edits through one repository-backed interface.
docs.spec.commands.title: Command surface
docs.spec.edits.body: Prefer small node operations over full-file rewrites. Writes fail on duplicate data-og-id or data-og-internal-id, invalid target scope, invalid editable attributes, or post-edit validation errors.
docs.spec.edits.title: Node edits
docs.spec.heading.title: The technical contract for editing OpenGraphite pages.
docs.spec.i18n.body: Binding text keeps readable HTML fallback plus data-i18n-key. The preferred source for localized text is public/locales/<locale>.json; preview mock state selects a variant but is not itself a text resource.
docs.spec.i18n.meta: i18n inspect / i18n resource set / text variant set
docs.spec.i18n.title: i18n resources
docs.spec.mcp.body: OpenGraphite MCP exposes resources and tools, but write tools—including migrate_project—delegate to ogkiln. AI clients therefore share the same dry-run proposal, stale guard, diagnostics, screenshots, and atomic write path as humans and CI.
docs.spec.mcp.title: MCP interface
docs.spec.nodes.body: OpenGraphite derives operation capabilities from standard tags, DOM content, native controls, ARIA, media/SVG/mask evidence, and computed display. Legacy classifications are removed only by the explicit migration workflow; ordinary inspection never rewrites source.
docs.spec.nodes.title: Editable nodes
docs.spec.place.body: component-placement hosts belong only in component canvases, and clone edits resolve to the source component node. .ogp previewContext.placementMocks uses host.<attribute> / host.class to project temporary standard attributes, classes, and ARIA onto the generated clone; authored :host(...) CSS decides computed state. The internal-ID entry is preferred, with display-ID fallback only when absent; both are never merged. data-og-*, on*, id, style, slot, and part are protected; source HTML and static builds stay unchanged. The Sample keeps code / preview / loading / collapsed states synchronized.
docs.spec.place.title: Placement mocks
docs.spec.refs.body: Agents should target copied ogref values. Pages use ogref:page:chapterInternalID:pageInternalID, components use ogref:component:collectionInternalID:componentInternalID, and nodes add the node internal ID.
docs.spec.refs.meta: data-og-id for display / data-og-internal-id for identity
docs.spec.refs.title: Reference IDs
docs.spec.scope.body: .ogp stores repository resolution, htmlRoot, Chapters, Collections, page/component entries, canvas placement, viewport size, and preview mock state. It does not duplicate DOM structure or design values.
docs.spec.scope.title: Project scope
docs.spec.slots.body: Component masters are standard Custom Element hosts whose template defines Shadow DOM, named slots, and exposed parts. Pages keep lightweight og-instance references and pass page-specific content with the standard slot attribute.
docs.spec.slots.title: Components and slots
docs.spec.source.body: HTML is the page DOM, CSS renders shared rules, assets and locale JSON stay as implementation resources, and runtime or build output is derived. OpenGraphite does not create another design IR.
docs.spec.source.title: Source model
docs.spec.verify.body: A legacy 0.1.0 Web contract is migrated only after a dry-run over the registered local HTML/CSS/runtime closure: review every diff and its proposalReference, then apply that same proposal. Ambiguous component, slot, placement state, import, or runtime dependencies are blocking and require manual standardization before another dry-run. The .ogp and Agent schema versions stay unchanged, project-local contract configuration is not a migration target, and preview state never enters source HTML. Validate, capture visual output, and run a deterministic static build after migration.
docs.spec.verify.title: Migrate, verify, and build

home.component.build.body: Spacing, order, and state remain attached to the page, so judgment made by a designer and judgment made with assistance meet in the same place.
home.component.build.title: People and tools read the same decisions.
home.component.runtime.body: Instead of polishing a disposable mock and rebuilding it later, OpenGraphite keeps design work close to the shape that continues forward.
home.component.runtime.title: Bring the canvas closer to the outcome.
home.component.title: Do not give every tool a different truth.
home.hero.lead: OpenGraphite keeps the place you shape an interface close to the place it continues to live. It reduces throwaway copies and keeps product decisions in one flow.
home.hero.scope: See it -> refine it -> keep it in place
home.hero.title: OpenGraphite
home.preview.title: OpenGraphite workspace
home.principles.agent.body: When work spreads beyond what can be seen, decisions become vague. OpenGraphite values changes that can be checked from the current view.
home.principles.agent.title: Stay accountable to what is visible
home.principles.runtime.body: A change should leave its intent close enough to be read later. OpenGraphite keeps the reason and the visible result from drifting apart.
home.principles.runtime.title: Leave decisions where they can be read
home.principles.source.body: The result of shaping the interface remains available for the next step. OpenGraphite avoids disposable copies and keeps work in one flow.
home.principles.source.title: Design where the work will remain
home.principles.title: OpenGraphite keeps product work from splitting into another truth.
